cultural.vision_reason: The image shows moulded unfired clay votive stupas (tsha-tsha), a standard Tibetan Buddhist devotional object; Monpa practice Tibetan-style Vajrayana Buddhism with texts in Tibetan script, so this is plausible for the culture even without specific attribution beyond "the monk who produced it."

physical.title: stupa; ts'a-ts'a
physical.summary: Ts'a-ts'a, or moulded and unfired clay votive stupa.  Formed with a central and uppermost miniature stupa, with below, concentric rings of smaller stupas.  According to the monk who produced it, the total number of stupas is the auspicious 108.  At the base of the stupa are two registers, the upper one of text in Tibetan characters and the lower one of lotus petals.  Below this is an extended and unmoulded element, made to extract the stupa itself from the mould and to stand it on when offered.  The whole thing, only with the exception of the bottom, has been lightly washed with white paint (in the past it would have been lime-wash; this is more like house paint).

cultural.vision_reason: Three small moulded clay votive stupas (tsa-tsa), ritual objects used in Tibetan Buddhist practice by the Monpa people; museum attributes production directly to Monpa makers.

physical.title: stupa; ts'a-ts'a
physical.summary: Small clay votive stupa, ts'a-ts'a.  Made of unfired clay pressed from a metal mould and, afterwards, dusted with blue powder paint.  Made up of a central upper dome (spire damaged) with, set on the flanks of the lower part, eight round-domed stupas with staircases.  All of this set on a lotus-petal base.  Below this is a tapering, undecorated element used to extract the moulded part from the mould, and for setting the stupa down on in the shrine.
